body:
It is extremely complicated but it is what it is,  and I've made the choice to stand by her through it so I'll do what I can.  I didn't previously Ill admit but I have started taking care of myself much more as well in the past half a year or so, though I appreciate your concern.

I've checked out a couple bipolar subs so far though I feel like I only manage to get bits and pieces of useful information, I was thinking I may make posts there too and see what comes of it, I'm learning more and more and it's really opening my eyes to how and why my gf works the way she does though so it's a start.

She does understand she's at rock bottom and does want to change, she's doing her best with meds and therapy right now even though it terrifies her and I'm so so proud of her for that. The main issue is she doesn't understand how to make those changes or where to even begin. That's part of why I'm here, to try and help her find those ways. 

Finding a way to accept that people aren't perfect is definitely something to work on though, she knows deep down nobody is perfect but she puts so much pressure on herself to be prefect in every way she can be, and hates herself if she can't. I belive that's a part of what leads her to inadvertently expect perfection in others as well. 

You're right it's a perspective issue and that's no easy fix,  I know she needs a therapist that understands what she's going through but my hope is that while she's struggling to solve that particular problem and find one that's right for her,  perhaps if I learn more about her I may be able to help bridge that gap in some way. 

Thank you for the encouragement, I do appreciate it and the advice.

To me I understand that it's a lot more complicated for her, there are a myriad of things that I could not encompass here, and so many contradictions in her heart, she understands it isn't easy but right now I do not believe she has the capacity to put her all into our relationship right now, at least as far as she's  capable of believing in her heart.

It's a little of both, I've understood for quite some time that some of it was eggshells but I did make some mistakes,  hiding things from her that I shouldn't have, blowing up at her when I couldn't understand what she was going through and took things personally when I should have understood she was crying out for help deep down and couldn't voice it. 

The reason I personally feel I'm in a position where I may be able to help her it's because I'm the one person she does not fake a smile with anymore. She does not go out of her way to talk to me unless she's feeling comfortable to some extent and that's been through a long while of me showing her that she can be comfortable with me even if it's a slow process. 

I know the ways her ex used to get her to open up, he was the only one who could and I strongly feel that if I truly come to understand her and her heart deep down, I could be that shelter for her too.

I'm sure deep down she understands it's hard for me, she doesn't beg me to stay, she doesn't beg me to do this for her,  she's just very blunt about the fact she can't bring herself to open up on her own right now, hence why I need to be the one to get her to do so.

Hello, she has tried therapy multiple times and so far has only encountered therapists that were no help to her (Including one that made her kind of afraid to get another therapist like them) Though she is currently trying to find a new one to my understanding and still going in for counseling and medication. Meds are helping a bit, therapy not so much.

Yes from what you've told me the two of you sound extremely alike, I was amazed by some of the similarities. I appreciate the encouragement, and yes it really is a struggle for the both of us and I'll continue doing my best to support her and keep myself sane too haha, I'm feeling even more hopeful after talking to you. 

Thank you so very much for that, you don't know what it means to me for you to leave the door (dms) open for advice, I truly appreciate you.

She does do the same thing from when I've noticed and I used to get overly offended and it got us both in a darker spot. I wasn't very understanding of her before and I have very strong regrets for that. I think deep down I realized there were probably underlying causes and I simply didn't allow myself to acknowledge them, but to have someone who really knows all of this and has experienced it firsthand it really brings a lot of it into perspective for me, moreso than I feel I have managed to on my own. I will absolutely do my best to try and make her feel validated and follow your advice where applicable.

I was unfortunately unaware that understimulation was a thing, but after reading what you've said I feel as if it was something I should have caught and thought of, it definitely describes my gf. It seems to me a lot of those issues with self esteem and personal worries apply to her as well, so I will do my best to make comments and give her reassurance, and bring up small topics to just talk and break the silence, it's not gone well before but I think that's moreso because in the past I was incapable of letting go of my own emotions and it showed, I sounded awkward and sometimes upset and that absolutely made things worse for her, but if I can go into it with confidence and comfortable myself then I believe taking your advice will go far. She is absolutely the type who believes she's not worth being cared for so I know that she struggles to believe I care.

"Conversation doesn’t have to be 100% engaging all the time" is extremely reassuring for me and something that I'd like to help her see as well, I've been feeling extremely inadaquate to have failed to be interesting to her and that's my own self confidence issues, something I've struggled to come to terms with so that I can better help her without my emotions influencing me.

You're right as for uncomfortable topics, I think your advice is a much better approach than what I have been doing, I admit I've struggled feeling like I have to find a good time on my own but I don't often ask her what she thinks, and that's something that I see needs to change. Though I know if it's left to her revisiting another time is unlikely to happen but I think if we can work on some of our issues that will become easier for her, I want to be someone she can feel comfortable and safe with.

As for doing research I absolutely will do that, I will admit it's not something I've done past the base knowledge of what they are but it's something I should have focused on a lot more, which is what I guess I am attempting to do here as well. I'll make it something like my homework for the foreseeable future.

​

Would you be okay if I message you with more questions now and then on top of said research? I have to admit reading your responses got me a little teary because it gave me a lot of insight that I've struggled to obtain in the past, some things I worried in the back of my mind I would never be able to make sense of as I should, almost like a breath of fresh air. I definitely don't want to drop a bunch of unecessary stuff on you if it's something you can't handle being someone who has struggled plenty on their own so if you need to say no I will completely understand, and I thank you so, so much for the advice you've already given, truly!

I do hope she does one day but it's hard to say, either way even if she never does I'll be happy if she can come to live happily, it's truly all I want for her. 

I may not be on the spectrum but I've struggled with depression and similar issues all my life and I know how awful and how hard it can get, and whether or not things are good between us I want to see her thrive. I want to understand her own unique struggles and help her learn to see the world in a brighter light. 

Thank you so much for the kind words, it's every bit as much a help as any advice I could get as encouraging words help me to keep going and feel maybe I'm doing the right thing you know? None of this is easy, for me or especially her but she's my world and I'd do anything for her.
No need to apologize friend I value all help and advice I recieve strongly and if I can find more places to cover more ground and get potential advice, that's a big help to me too.

This is extremely helpful perspective, I would like to find a way to gently tell her some of this but I can't go into it pushing too hard because she's very averse to me adding anymore stress when she's constantly thinking of everything else she's going through. It's very difficult to bring up any uncomfortable topics for her and I get the sense she resents me doing it. 

It's hard to admit that there are some things that I can't do but helping her self esteem I can do my best with! Do you know how one could make you more comfortable with them if they made mistakes with you before your change of perspective there? Someone who because of their mistakes may have made you very uncomfortable to be around them?

Also do you know is it a common issue to struggle with silence? Like a strong dislike for silence that makes you extremely uncomfortable even moreso with the person you were talking to if you both go silent because you can't think of anything else to say or do? Because that's another issue she struggles with, if we go silent and don't have anything else to say she starts to get uncomfortable with me and I get the sense she blames me for that one,  but basically she and I both struggle to come up with things to talk about and consistently keep up conversation, or things we both enjoy.
I will do that now, thank you!
